category_title: Pupils who 'show off' and struggle with impulse control in peer groups
scenario_title: Reflecting on peer conflict and showing off in a support group
minimal_context: David is participating in a support group discussion to reflect on a recent conflict where he was showing off in front of his friends.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: David, let's look back at the situation where you were showing off in front of your friends. Once you had time to calm down, what did you lose from the situation?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Why did you feel less confident?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What made you do those things when your friends were there?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Don’t know. I’ll admit this. I know I’m no’ a pure angel in class but I can behave when I want to behave.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: David, let's look back at the situation where you were showing off in front of your friends. Once you had time to calm down, what did you lose from the situation?

STUDENT: Confidence.

TUTOR: Why did you feel less confident?

STUDENT: Because I’d done bad things.

TUTOR: What made you do those things when your friends were there?

STUDENT: Don’t know. I’ll admit this. I know I’m no’ a pure angel in class but I can behave when I want to behave.

task.content: Reflect upon a past experience in which there was conflict and to identify the gains and losses (not only pertaining to themselves personally) which arose from the situation, and then to respond to the question: 'What would you do differently if you were faced with the same situation again?'
task.learning_goal: Promote reflection and discussion to achieve an understanding of the forces upon their behaviour and how such understanding can inform future behaviour

context.environment: Collaborative support group activity where a common feature is that there are no worksheets
context.materials: Transcript derived from video-camera footage, scenarios, card sorts, prioritisation exercises
context.social_setting: Group discussion with a Support Group Leader (SGL) and other members of the group
context.time_context: Once the pupil had time to calm down after a situation

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When the Support Group Leader asks the pupil to explain the underlying reason for their feelings (e.g., 'Why did you feel less confident?') after they admitted losing confidence
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Gives a vague, dismissive response ('Don't know') while simultaneously asserting capacity for self-control ('I can behave when I want to behave')
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Feels a loss of confidence because they had 'done bad things', but does not understand why they behave in the ways that they do
related_quotes: I’ll admit this. I know I’m no’ a pure angel in XXXX but I can behave when I want to behave.

behavior_patterns.internal_state: Cannot control behavior when under pressure or when they want to

behavior_patterns.condition: When facing potential conflict situations like a reprimand in the classroom
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Becomes rude, resentful, angry, agitated, argumentative, bad-tempered and/or confrontational, resulting in a tantrum
related_quotes: Any situation like this results in a tantrum from . . .
